messages:
marta: Heads-up — running the sampleapp against staging today I saw stream fragments arrive out of order after a short net flap. App concatenates SSE chunks and sometimes we get JSON parse errors.

oliver: ugh. can you repro reliably? sampleapp or our browser SDK?

marta: sampleapp (node example) using the eventsource wrapper. Happens after a connection resume — seems like the last-fragment of the previous connection and first-fragment of the resumed connection are interleaved. Not sure if it's server-side chunk boundary or client buffer reassembly bug.

raj: do you have raw response chunks? headers + body? that'd help. also which retry strategy on the client?

marta: repro steps: 1) start sampleapp stream -> 2) use `tc qdisc` to drop packets for 200ms -> 3) restore. Observed ~1/15 streams fail with `Unexpected token` during JSON.parse. I have a capture:```
id: 42
data: {"delta":"hello"}



id: 43
data: {"delta":"world"}
``` then resumed chunks look like:```


data: {"delta":"wo



"
``` which ends up merged into previous partial token.

emily: that looks like boundary markers (`\n\n`) not being respected when concatenating buffers on resume. In browser we rely on `lastEventId` + event separater parsing; node's stream reassembly code might be trimming leading newlines.

oliver: @marta can you attach the sampleapp trace/stack + Node version? we've seen subtle Buffer pooling causing leading newline to be dropped before we parse.

marta: node 18.17.1, sampleapp commit 7a2b. Trace: `Error: Unexpected token \n in JSON at position 0` from our SSE handler at parseSseChunk (src/sse/parse.js:87). I can paste handler.

raj: paste it, but also try adding explicit `\n\n` normalization before feeding chunks to parse logic as a quick fix.

marta: parse snippet: ```js
function onData(buf){
  buffer += buf.toString('utf8');
  // naive split by \n\n

  const parts = buffer.split('\n\n');
  buffer = parts.pop() || '';
  parts.forEach(p => handleEvent(p));
}
```

kai: yeah that naive split will choke if you get spurious blank lines or half-delimiters across chunk boundaries. We should use a streaming parser that treats `\r?\n\r?\n` as separator and preserves leading blanks on new connection. Also preserve last-event-id and attach it to resumed requests.

emily: another angle: our resume flow currently prepends the buffered tail (partial event) to the new connection's first chunk. If the first chunk starts with extra newlines, concatenation can create `\n\n\n` sequences that `split('\n\n')` turns into an empty part that becomes invalid JSON.

oliver: sounds like two fixes: 1) more robust split (regex \r?\n\r?\n) and trim only the exact separators, not arbitrary leading whitespace; 2) add a small unit test in sampleapp simulating netem flaps to ensure no parse regressions.

marta: I can prototype the split change and a tiny netem test harness. Any objections to a quick patch?

raj: go for it. also add a non-destructive logging flag `--sse-debug` to sampleapp so we can dump raw chunks for postmortem without flooding logs by default.

deploy-bot: build queued for branch marta/sse-reassembly-fix (CI: sampleapp-unit).

emily: once we have a repro, let's add a cross-sdk test in our streaming parity suite (node + browser + python) that injects an artificial boundary in the middle of an event. That will catch this across runtimes.

marta: ok will open PR with: minimal parser change, `--sse-debug` flag, netem test script, and a follow-up ticket to add cross-sdk parity test. Adding the failing capture to the PR.

oliver: thanks — please link the ticket to the streaming-evals epic and ping me for review. :thumbsup:

marta: will do. thanks everyone!
